key_insight: IMPACT combines inverter-level cloud dynamics with plant history, solar geometry, and weather to improve 10–110-minute-ahead probabilistic photovoltaic power forecasts.
engineering_relevance: More accurate, calibrated short-term solar forecasts could support grid balancing and operational planning under changing cloud conditions.
method: Encode four input branches, including inverter dynamics via graph attention with learned adjacency, and fuse them through gated cross-attention.
Augment solar geometry with horizon-weighted cloud heterogeneity and inverter ramp-down signals.
Learn horizon-conditioned corrections to smart persistence, then calibrate quantiles online using kernel-weighted adaptive conformal calibration.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an FSS of 0.2950, outperforming all 14 baselines by at least 0.099, with positive contributions from every branch and FSS values of 0.198 under overcast and 0.255 under variable skies.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify dataset size or cross-site validation, leaving generalization to other photovoltaic plants uncertain.
paper_title: IMPACT: Inverter-Informed Multimodal Learning for Photovoltaic Generation Forecasting
